tagline: Leading Nordic financial services group serving millions of customers across the region
hero_kpi_rationale: Nordea reports high and stable profitability, with an ROE of 15.4% in Q1 2026, well above the expected 15% threshold for the year. This KPI is central to the evaluation of European banks and reflects the efficiency of the business model despite adverse conditions.

kpis.name: Return on Equity
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by average shareholders' equity, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: A high and sustained ROE indicates strong profit generation from equity. Nordea maintains a high level despite lower policy rates.
kpis.signal: ROE stable at 15.4%, despite volatile markets.

kpis.name: Cost-to-Income Ratio
kpis.explanation: Operating costs divided by operating income, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: The ratio deteriorated to 45.5% from 43.7% last year, primarily due to weaker market revenues, but remains below the 46% threshold.
kpis.signal: Slight deterioration due to lower market revenues.

kpis.name: Net Interest Income
kpis.explanation: Difference between interest earned and interest paid by the bank.
kpis.description: Net interest income declined 4% year-on-year, in line with expectations, due to a lower interest rate environment.
kpis.signal: Expected decline linked to lower policy rates.

kpis.name: Operating Profit
kpis.description: Operating profit reached €1.634 Bn, up 2% year-on-year, supported by fee growth and loss management.

kpis.name: Net Loan Losses
kpis.explanation: Amount provisioned for doubtful loans, net of reversals.
kpis.description: Net loan losses were negative (reversal) at €99M, as Nordea released €160M in excess provisions.
kpis.signal: Reversal of €99M due to release of management buffer.

kpis.name: CET1 Ratio
kpis.explanation: Key measure of bank financial strength, reflecting high-quality capital.
kpis.description: The CET1 ratio stands at 15.7%, reflecting robust capital generation and prudent balance sheet management.
kpis.signal: Very strong capital position, 1.9 percentage points above regulatory minimum.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 10.4823 SEK in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of 3.268 Bn SEK in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 67.5% in the latest year.

kpis.name: Mortgage Lending Growth
kpis.explanation: Annual growth in mortgage loans granted to individuals.
kpis.description: Mortgage lending increased 2% year-on-year, driven by demand in Sweden and Norway.
kpis.signal: Sustained growth in Sweden and Norway.

kpis.name: Corporate Lending Growth
kpis.explanation: Annual growth in loans granted to corporations.
kpis.description: Corporate lending surged 11%, supported by strong activity across all Nordic markets.
kpis.signal: Very strong momentum across all countries.

kpis.name: Assets Under Management
kpis.explanation: Total value of assets managed on behalf of clients.
kpis.description: Assets under management reached €464 Bn, up 9%, with positive net flows in private banking.

risks.title: Geopolitical conflicts and Nordic recession
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned at the beginning of the section with strong language ('could trigger'), describing material impact on growth, investments, and employment. Emerging/increased trend given 2026 context. Geopolitical category carries high weight for a Nordic bank.

risks.title: Equity market correction and AI valuations
risks.score_rationale: Positioned early in risk factors with language indicating material impact ('could further weigh on'). New/increased risk related to growing concerns over AI valuations. Affects business and consumer confidence, a major macroeconomic criterion.

risks.title: Credit risk and insufficient provisions
risks.score_rationale: Positioned centrally in the report with detailed quantitative data (EUR 76m adjustments, EUR 160m released). Technical language revealing major post-model approach revision. Trend increasing: full deployment of judgmental provisions. Credit category carries high weight for a bank.

risks.title: Direct exposure to Russian counterparties
risks.score_rationale: Specific risk explicitly mentioned with declared ongoing monitoring. Exposure reduced (less than EUR 20m after provisions) but active surveillance indicates persistent risk. Trend stable but within an intensified geopolitical context. High weight for a Nordic bank.

risks.title: Deterioration in commercial real estate portfolio
risks.score_rationale: Detailed data shows Stage 2 and 3 exposures in real estate (EUR 1,608m in Stage 2-3 vs EUR 1,621m at end-2025). 'Retail trade' sector shows high provisions (EUR 111m). Trend stable but vulnerable to adverse scenarios (real estate price decline -6.1% in Denmark). High credit weight.

risks.title: High unemployment in Finland and consumption
risks.score_rationale: Scenario data shows Finnish unemployment at 10.3-11.7% (vs 8.1-11.4% in Sweden), with negative consumption in adverse scenario (-1.3%). Positioned in detailed provisioning tables. Trend stable but structurally high. Impact on Finnish credit portfolio (EUR 580m provisions).

risks.title: Concentration in real estate and construction sectors
risks.score_rationale: Real estate represents EUR 45,921m (15% of portfolio), construction EUR 8,121m with provisions of EUR 95m. Combined, real estate-construction exposure totals EUR 54m. Trend stable but vulnerable to real estate price shocks. High weight for a Nordic bank.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or its applications in the provided documents. Nordea does not position AI as a strategic lever in its recent communications.
evidence: No reference to AI, generative models, or advanced automation tools
Absence of KPIs related to AI adoption or AI APIs
Focus on basic digitalization (onboarding, app usage) without mention of advanced technology
